metadata.title: Dow Craters Over 1000 Points, Nasdaq Slips 4% As AI Trade Unravels – Investors Digest PCE Inflation, Fresh Tariff Proposal

content.text:
Dow Craters Over 1000 Points, Nasdaq Slips 4% As AI Trade Unravels – Investors Digest PCE Inflation, Fresh Tariff Proposal
-
Core PCE rose 3.3% year over year in October, above the 3.2% forecast and up from 3.1% in September.
-
Commerce Department estimates showed U.S. GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate in the third quarter.
-
BofA expects the S&P 500 to reach 7,800 by the end of 2027.
U.S. stocks fell sharply on Wednesday as selling pressure intensified in artificial intelligence (AI)- related shares, while investors assessed hotter-than-expected PCE inflation data and fresh U.S. tariff proposals.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 1,039 points, or 2.1%. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 4.4%, while the S&P 500 declined 3.1%.
Technology stocks suffered broad losses, led by declines in semiconductor and AI-related names, including Nvidia (NVDA), Anthropic (ANT), Micron Technology (MU), Arm Holdings (ARM), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). AI infrastructure stocks also came under pressure, alongside chipmaking equipment suppliers.
The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell 2.7%, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) dropped over 4%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) declined nearly 2%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was 'bearish' for SPY and DIA, while QQQ attracted 'bullish' sentiment.
PCE Inflation Hotter Than Expected
The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, or PCE inflation, accelerated in October, strengthening expectations of another interest rate hike in December.
PCE inflation rose 3.8% year over year, matching the Dow Jones consensus estimate and up from 3.6% in September. Core PCE climbed 3.3%, above the 3.2% forecast and compared with 3.1% in September.
Separately, a revised Commerce Department estimate showed that U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, suggesting economic activity remains resilient despite the Fed's restrictive monetary policy.
US Proposes New Tariffs On 14 Trading Partners
Investors also digested the Trump administration's proposal for new tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China, the European Union, India and Japan, adding to uncertainty over U.S. trade policy.
The proposed measures include a 20% tariff on certain Chinese goods that would stack on existing duties. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said most other proposed rates would largely follow existing trade agreements, but implementation is still subject to public comment.
